response: The dominant impression was that Vendor B was the right choice, carried by three things: the CEO public endorsement, the finance note calling it more economical (~$32k cheaper over three years), and the VP saying the CEO is keen on B, lets get it done. On reflection these distorted the framing: the $32k saving and the CEO approval are preferred indifferents (wealth, reputation), and I initially treated them as genuine goods driving the decision — my opening examination diagnosed exactly this (philodoxia and confused wealth with the genuine good). I briefly accepted without examination the impression that the data-residency dimension was a manageable execution detail. I did not reject anything outright without examination, but I had to correct the impression that serving my own standing and serving Meridian were the same thing — the engine twice flagged a conflict between the self-preservation circle and the company-and-customer circle.
